css:
.vec::after { content:"\2192"; position:absolute; left:0; right:0; top:-.66em;
              font-size:.6em; text-align:center; line-height:1; font-style:normal; }

.sqb { border-top:1.4px solid #1f2430; padding:0 4px 0 1px; margin-left:-1px;
       display:inline-block; line-height:1; }

/* THE NOTATION FACE: LESS SLANT, A LITTLE MORE WEIGHT. EVERY SUBJECT.
   `.m`/`.dm` were Times New Roman ITALIC. Times's italic is steeply
   slanted and, at this size, very light — and the page prints at
   PRINT_ZOOM 0.734, which thins it again. Beside the Hindi prose (a solid
   sans) every equation read as faint and tilted.

   Deliberately NOT scoped to a subject. The notation is the same object
   in every chapter — physics sets 490 display equations, chemistry its
   formulae, biology the occasional ratio — and scoping the face to maths
   would mean the SAME `$f(x)$` rendered two different ways depending on
   which chapter it appeared in. That is the class of inconsistency the
   callout-icon rule exists to prevent elsewhere: a property of the
   element, not of the chapter it sits in.

   Two changes, both small:

   1. Charter's italic is a far more upright cut than Times's, with lining
      figures matching the `font-variant-numeric:lining-nums` already set
      on `.m`. Variables stay italic — correct maths typography, and the
      upright digits/operators (`.up`) are untouched — they just no longer
      lean off the line. Times stays in the stack as the fallback, so a
      machine without Charter renders exactly as before. Pagination is
      safe either way because the packer MEASURES with this same
      stylesheet in the same browser that renders it.

   2. `-webkit-text-stroke` rather than `font-weight`. The next real weight
      up is 700 — far too heavy for running notation, and it would change
      every glyph's advance width and so re-measure every line. A 0.2px
      stroke thickens the strokes just enough to match the prose's colour
      without moving anything, the same reason the book sets its Kalam
      bold synthetically.

   CHEMISTRY KEEPS ITS UPRIGHT POSTURE. `.subj-chemistry .m/.dm` sets
   `font-style:normal` (an element symbol is roman: SOCl2, not slanted),
   and nothing here sets `font-style`, so that rule is unaffected —
   chemistry gains the face and the weight and stays upright.

   Applied to the nested levels too (`.fr`, matrix cells), or a fraction
   inside an equation would be the one thin, slanted thing left on the
   page. */
.m, .dm, .fr, .mx>.mxg>span {
    font-family:Charter,'Bitstream Charter','Iowan Old Style',
                'Times New Roman',Times,serif;
    -webkit-text-stroke:.2px currentColor; }
/* The `.k` equation label is a reference, not notation — already upright
   and 700, and a stroke on top of that turns it to a blob. */
.dm>.k { -webkit-text-stroke:0; }
